question: What percentage of carbon does the Earth's crust have in the form of minerals?
solution:
The **correct** answer is **0.02%**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Only 0.02% of the **carbon** in the crust of the **Earth** is present as **carbonates**, hydrogen carbonates, **coal**, and petroleum.
 
• **Mineral** elements include **carbon**.
 
• In order for **fossil fuels **like coal and **petroleum** to function, **carbon** must be present.
 
• All of the **carbonate minerals** that make up **limestone** and **dolomite**, as well as the minerals made entirely of carbon, such as **graphite** and **diamond**, contain it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Formation of Earth Crust.
 
 
• The **most prevalent** elements in the crust are **oxygen** and **silicon**.
 
• Both **oceanic** and **continental** crusts make up the surface of the Earth.
 
• Despite being the most prevalent minerals in both crusts, **silicates** nonetheless have some unique features.
 
• **Shale**, sandstone, and **limestone **make up the remaining 4%,** 0.75%**, 0.75, and 95 percent of the crust of the Earth. Igneous and **metamorphic rocks** make up the remaining 4%.
 
• The Earth's crust is made up of **90 different **elements, with oxygen, silicon, **aluminum, **and iron making up **88.1%** of its **mass**.
